issues.body: The document commits a full table of work-box byte counts, microsecond timings, ratios, percentages, and noise estimates, then repeats derived figures throughout the findings and disposition. The repository contract explicitly prohibits hard-coded performance numbers in Markdown and says work-box timings are non-canonical. Labeling them advisory/non-canonical does not make committing them compliant. These values can also become stale while continuing to look authoritative.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the numeric table and all derived hard-coded magnitudes (including percentages, ratios, microseconds, spread, and exact byte/capacity observations). Keep the qualitative negative conclusion, methodology, reproducible commands, result-equivalence evidence, and a pointer to generated benchmark artifacts if such artifacts are available through the approved benchmark workflow.
issues.title: Committed Markdown contains prohibited hard-coded work-box performance numbers

verdict.summary: The feature implementation and cross-arm correctness test are plausibly sound, but the change violates the repository's explicit evidence policy by committing hard-coded, non-canonical work-box performance measurements to Markdown. The caveats do not cure that prohibition. Remove the recorded timings and derived numeric comparisons, retaining only the qualitative measured conclusion and reproducible harness.
